newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: ANZ BANK TO CUT EXPORT REFINANCE RATE IN PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: ANZ BANK TO CUT EXPORT REFINANCE RATE IN PAKISTAN.

text.p: ANZ Grindlays Bank Pakistan said on Thursday it would lower its export refinance interest rate to 10 percent from 11 to boost exports with effect from August 14, Pakistan's 50th anniversary of independence.

"This will be the lowest rate available in Pakistan," Azhar Hamid, general manager of ANZ Grindlays Bank Pakistan told a news conference. "We hope the bank's export financiing will triple after this decision...If all the banks do the same, all exporters will benefit," he said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan lowered its export refinance rates to 11 percent from 13 last month.
Hamid said ANZ Grindlay's initiative was in line with the government's economic reforms and would help Pakistan achieve its target of 15 percent export growth in 1997/98 (July-June).
Pakistan's trade deficit stood at $3.373 billion in 1996/97 compared to $3.666 billion in 1995/96.
Hamid said Pakistan's exports were lagging in an extremely competive international market.

"There is need for improved quality and productivity, lower input costs and reduced cost of finance," he said. "With a massive 23 percent reduction in borrowing cost, the exporters are expected to respond positively so that the 1998 export growth target of 15 percent is not only met but surpassed."
Hamid said recent decisions by the government had addressed some of the key issues for exporters.
"Under the export refinance scheme, the exporters may borrow funds for up to 50 percent of their annual exports. The cost of such borrowing will now be reduced from 13 to 10 percent.
"If the profit margin for an exporter was previously 10 percent, he will immediately benefit by at least 15 percent higher profit resulting from this reduction of borrowing cost."
Hamid said he hoped the exporters would pass on some of the improved margin to their foreign buyers to make exports more attractive.
